items.excerpt: Hands-on with Lightcraft's Spark Story, unveiled at SIGGRAPH 2026: a screenplay-first virtual production tool that lets writers, directors and cinematographers build and shoot a virtual film set — recording shots with just an iPhone — long before any physical location or set exists.

At SIGGRAPH 2026 NVIDIA rolled out agentic AI for creative pros, with Model Context Protocol integrations that let AI assistants act inside Adobe, Blender, Unreal Engine and other design apps — inspecting scenes, flagging color issues and preparing export variants while artists keep creative control.

A developer called VoxelKei released 'inversphere,' a technique that folds entire 360-degree environments into a single sphere for displaying 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes — a novel capture-and-display approach feeding real-time 3D and render workflows.

Argues that piling more words into AI image prompts yields diminishing returns, and that supplying visual style references gives designers far more reliable, repeatable control over generated output — a practical shift in creative-AI craft.

Makes the case that every AI chatbot has an implicit information architecture whether or not anyone designed it, and shows how UX designers can map a bot's capabilities and decision paths like a sitemap to make conversational products coherent.

Walks through why LLM-generated UI in Cursor and Bolt lands in an uncanny valley of functional-but-generic layouts, and offers concrete prompt and design-system fixes to push AI output past the tell-tale defaults.
